verses.1:1: And the word of the LORD came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,
verses.1:2: "Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim against it, for their wickedness has ascended before Me."
verses.1:3: But Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish; so he paid its fare and went down into it to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
verses.1:4: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and a great tempest arose on the sea, so that the ship seemed about to break apart.
verses.1:5: Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried out to his god, and they hurled the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten the weight upon them. Meanwhile, Jonah had gone down into the lowest parts of the vessel, had lain down, and had fallen into a deep sleep.
verses.1:6: So the captain drew near to him and said to him, "What is the matter with you, O sleeper? Arise, call upon your God! Perhaps God will give thought to us, so that we may not perish."
verses.1:7: And each man said to his companion, "Come, let us cast lots, that we may know on whose account this calamity has come upon us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.
verses.1:8: Then they said to him, "Tell us, please, on whose account has this calamity come upon us? What is your occupation, and from where do you come? What is your country, and of what people are you?"
verses.1:9: And he replied to them, "I am a Hebrew; it is the LORD, the God of heaven, whom I fear, who made the sea and the dry land."
verses.1:10: Then the men feared with a great fear and said to him, "What is this that you have done?" For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
verses.1:11: Then they said to him, "What shall we do to you, that the sea may grow calm for us?" For the sea was growing ever more tempestuous.
verses.1:12: And he said to them, "Lift me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will grow calm for you; for I know that it is on my account that this great tempest is upon you."
verses.1:13: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to turn back to the dry land, but they were not able, for the sea kept growing ever more tempestuous against them.
verses.1:14: Therefore they cried out to the LORD and said, "We pray, O LORD, do not let us perish for the life of this man, and do not lay innocent blood upon us; for You, O LORD, have done as it pleased You."
verses.1:15: So they lifted up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its fury.
verses.1:16: Then the men feared the LORD with a great fear, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and vowed vows.
verses.2:1: Now the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained within the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
verses.2:2: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from within the belly of the fish.
verses.2:3: And he said, "Out of my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me; from the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and You heard my voice.
verses.2:4: For You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the flood encompassed me; all Your breakers and Your billows swept over me.
verses.2:5: And I said, 'I have been driven away from before Your eyes,' yet I shall again gaze toward Your holy temple.
verses.2:6: The waters closed in upon me, even to my soul; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was bound about my head.
verses.2:7: To the bases of the mountains I descended; the earth with its bars closed behind me forever. Yet You brought up my life from the pit, O LORD my God.
verses.2:8: When my soul grew faint within me, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer reached You, into Your holy temple.
verses.2:9: Those who cling to vain idols forsake their own lovingkindness.
verses.2:10: But I, with the voice of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to You; what I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the LORD!"
verses.2:11: Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out upon the dry land.
verses.3:1: And the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time, saying,
verses.3:2: "Arise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I speak to you."
verses.3:3: So Jonah arose and went to Nineveh according to the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was a great city before God, a journey of three days.
verses.3:4: And Jonah began to enter the city a journey of one day, and he cried out and said, "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!"
verses.3:5: And the men of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.
verses.3:6: When the word reached the king of Nineveh, he arose from his throne, laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat upon ashes.
verses.3:7: And he issued a proclamation and announced in Nineveh, by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, "Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them neither graze nor drink water.
verses.3:8: Rather, let both man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and let them cry out mightily to God; let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.
verses.3:9: Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn away from His fierce wrath, so that we may not perish."
verses.3:10: Then God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented concerning the calamity that He had said He would do to them, and He did not do it.
verses.4:1: Yet it was exceedingly displeasing to Jonah, and he burned with anger.
verses.4:2: Then he prayed to the LORD and said, "O LORD, I pray, was this not my word while I was still in my own land? Therefore I made haste to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that You are a gracious and merciful God, slow to anger and great in lovingkindness, who relents from bringing calamity.
verses.4:3: And now, O LORD, please take my life from me, for my death is better than my life."
verses.4:4: And the LORD said, "Is it well for you to be angry?"
verses.4:5: Then Jonah went out from the city and sat to the east of the city; and he made a booth for himself there and sat beneath it in the shade, until he should see what would happen in the city.
verses.4:6: And the LORD God appointed a plant, and it grew up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his distress. And Jonah rejoiced over the plant with great joy.
verses.4:7: But God appointed a worm at the rising of the dawn on the next day, and it struck the plant so that it withered.
verses.4:8: And it came to pass, when the sun rose, that God appointed a scorching east wind; and the sun struck upon Jonah's head so that he grew faint. And he asked for himself that he might die, and said, "My death is better than my life."
verses.4:9: Then God said to Jonah, "Is it well for you to be angry over the plant?" And he said, "It is well for me to be angry, even to death!"
verses.4:10: And the LORD said, "You have had compassion on the plant for which you did not labor, nor did you make it grow, which came to be in a night and perished in a night.
verses.4:11: And should I not have compassion on Nineveh, the great city, in which are more than one hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left, and much livestock?"

notes.1:4: The Hebrew verb translated 'hurled' recurs across chapter 1 for the LORD hurling the wind (1:4), the mariners hurling the cargo (1:5), and finally hurling Jonah into the sea (1:12, 1:15). The clause 'seemed about to break apart' literally personifies the ship as reckoning or thinking itself about to break.
notes.1:6: The rare Hebrew verb translated 'give thought' appears only here in the Hebrew Bible and expresses an Aramaic-related idiom for taking considerate care.
notes.1:16: The Hebrew expression 'feared the LORD with a great fear' uses a cognate accusative that echoes the sailors' earlier terror (1:10) while marking its transformation into reverent worship.
notes.2:1: In the Masoretic Hebrew text, chapter 2 begins here; most English versions number this verse as 1:17 and number Hebrew 2:2-11 as 2:1-10. The verb 'appointed' recurs in chapter 4 for the plant, the worm, and the east wind.
notes.2:2: Here the Hebrew briefly shifts from the masculine noun for fish (2:1, 2:11) to the feminine form.
notes.2:6: The Hebrew noun rendered 'soul' can also denote the throat or neck, conveying both waters rising to the throat and peril to life itself.
notes.2:9: The phrase 'their own lovingkindness' refers either to the covenant mercy of God that idolaters forfeit or to the loyal devotion they owe to Him.
notes.3:3: The Hebrew phrase 'a great city before God' (literally 'great to God') serves as a superlative for extraordinary size while also suggesting Nineveh's importance in God's sight.
notes.3:4: The Hebrew participle translated 'shall be overthrown' commonly denotes sudden destruction, as of Sodom, yet it also carries the sense of being turned around or transformed.
notes.3:10: The Hebrew verb 'relented' (also in 3:9) expresses God's compassionate turning back from threatened judgment in response to Nineveh's turning from its evil way.
notes.4:4: The Hebrew idiom combines the infinitive absolute meaning doing well or rightly with the expression for burning anger, questioning whether Jonah has any right to be angry, and is echoed verbatim in 4:9.
notes.4:6: The Hebrew word qiqayon appears only in Jonah 4 and denotes a fast-growing, broad-leaved plant, commonly identified as the castor-oil plant or a gourd vine.
notes.4:8: The rare Hebrew adjective charishit occurs only here and is understood to describe a scorching, sultry, or fierce east wind.
notes.4:10: Literally "son of a night," a Hebrew idiom expressing that the plant came into existence in a single night and perished just as rapidly.
